leftEvidence.role: Law, righteousness, and the inner life
leftEvidence.title: A divorce writing is set beside resulting adultery

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Jesus recalls the requirement of a divorce writing and speaks about putting away a wife.
points.right: Jesus recalls the murder command and extends danger of judgment to anger and contemptuous speech.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: An exception is named, and later marriages are described through adultery language.
points.right: A worshiper must seek reconciliation, and an adversary must be addressed before judgment closes the opportunity.

payload.posture: Both sayings move from remembered legal instruction into present relational consequence.

rightEvidence.role: Law, righteousness, and the inner life
rightEvidence.title: Murder language reaches anger, speech, and reconciliation

payload.tension: Reconciliation is commanded in one case while the compressed divorce saying names no equivalent repair process.
payload.title: Broken relationship, legal action, and repair
